pressReleaseTitle: India Ratings Affirms B.G. Shirke Construction Technology at ‘IND A’/Stable
issuerName: B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd.
overview: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) has affirmed B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd’s (BGSCTPL) Long-Term Issuer Rating at ‘IND A’. The Outlook is Stable. The instrument-wise rating actions are as follows:
overviewHTML: Ind-Ra continues to consider BGSCPTL’s standalone financials to arrive at the ratings and has not consolidated the amount of guarantee extended to its related parties such as B G Shirke Redevelopment and Gas Pvt. Ltd. (BGSRGPL), Parijat Hill View Realty LLP (PHVR) and Teenmurthy Summit Realty LLP (TSRLLP). However, Ind-Ra has factored in the debt guaranteed of these entities and any incremental support required by them to arrive at the ratings.
keyRatingDrivers:
Healthy Revenue Visibility: BGSCPTL maintained a healthy unexecuted order book of INR159.6 billion at end-December 2020 (end-October 2019: INR177.0 billion), providing a revenue visibility of 4.1x of FY20 revenues (5.2x). The company saw revenue growth of 6.8% yoy to INR38.7 billion in FY20 (FY19: 17.1% yoy). However, given the COVID-19-related impact and the slow order inflows from customers, the revenues are likely to drop to INR28 billion in FY21. For 9MFY21, the company recorded revenues of INR19.1 billion. Ind-Ra expects the pace of order execution to have picked up from 3QFY21 with a gradual improvement seen from 2QFY21; the company is likely to see healthy revenue growth in FY22.

 

Stable EBITDA Margins: The company’s EBITDA margin remained healthy and almost unchanged year-on-year at 20% in FY20. BGSCTPL has a price escalation clause for a majority of its contracts, thus protecting its margins from the fluctuations in the cost of key raw material such as steel and cement, which account for 30%-35% of the company’s total operating cost. The company recorded an EBITDA margin of 19.6% in 1HFY21. However, given the likely decline in the revenue in FY21, the margin could moderate to about 15% due to the lower absorption of fixed cost. The margins could, however, improve in FY22 due to the pick-up in order execution.

 

Comfortable Credit Metrics: BGSCTPL's on-balance sheet debt remained stable at INR10.2 billion at end-1HFY21, after falling 2.6% yoy to INR10.9 billion in FY20. This was led by the reduced outstanding cash credit limits. Given the reduced EBITDA levels in 1HFY21, the net leverage (net on-balance sheet debt/operating EBITDAR) marginally rose to 1.57x post an improvement to 0.95x in FY20 (FY19: 1.27x) and the gross interest coverage (operating EBITDAR/gross interest expense) reduced to 2.4x post an improvement to 4.10x (3.37x). The company did not avail any moratorium/deferments allowed by the Reserve Bank of India.

 

BGSCTPL extended a corporate guarantee to PHVR for INR0.31 billion in 1HFY21 (FY20: INR0.48 billion (includes INR0.17 billion to BGSRGPL and INR0.31 billion to PHVR), FY19: INR0.30 billion) and a letter of undertaking to TSRLLP for INR0.31 billion (0.53 billion, INR0.8 billion). Although adjusted gross debt fell 18% yoy to INR9.7 billion in 1HFY21 (FY20: INR11.9 billion, FY19: INR12.3 billion), the net adjusted leverage (adjusted net debt/operating EBITDAR) stood at 1.69x (1.09x; 1.42x), due to the reduced EBITDA. 

 

Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL’s  net leverage to remain at 1.4x-1.6x in FY21 due to the reduced EBITDA and gradually improve over the medium term on a rise in the EBITDA levels from FY22 and a limited increase in debt. 

 

Liquidity Indicator - Adequate: BGSCTPL had unencumbered cash and cash equivalents of INR3.9 billion in 1HFY21 (FY20: INR3.5 billion and FY19: INR2.2 billion) while the encumbered cash balance stood at INR1.2 billion at FYE20. Moreover, the maximum and average utilisation of its fund-based working capital limits stood at 11% and 28%, respectively, and that of its non-fund-based limits was 80% over the 12 months ended December 2020. The company’s fund-based and non-fund-based limits are largely from public sector banks and have limited presence of private banks.

 

The total gross debt of INR10.2 billion at end-1HFY21 comprised INR7.2 billion terms loan, INR0.75 billion intercorporate deposits and INR2.3 billion working capital loans. The company has INR1.98 billion and INR1.96 billion repayments due over FY22 and FY23, respectively.  BGSCTPL has a well-managed working capital cycle with receivable days of 40 in FY20 (FY19: 27).  BGSCTPL’s liquidity position improved during FY20, given the receipt of the pending dues from Telangana Rajiv Swagruha Corporation Limited totalling INR1.6 billion. The management expects the balance INR0.8 billion in FY21 with INR0.4 billion already received in December 2020.

 

Healthy Free Cash Flow: BGSCPTL’s cash flow from operations improved to INR4.1 billion in FY20 (FY19: INR1.7 billion) due to the limited outflow on working capital as the company managed its increased inventory through higher mobilisation advances (FY20: INR7.6 billion, FY19: INR7.4 billion) and advance from customers (INR2.8 billion, INR0.6 billion). The mobilisation advance from Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MAHADA) and City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) does not entail an interest pay out while those from Delhi Development Authority (DDA) carry an interest. Moreover, given the reduced capex of INR2.0 billion in FY20 (FY19: INR2.5 billion), the free cash flow turned positive in FY20 after being negative consistently for three years. The net working capital days stood at 21 at end-1HFY21 (FYE20: 25, FYE19: 20).  The company is likely to incur  capex of INR1.5 billion-2 billion each year over near term. Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL to report a fall in the cash flow from operations in FY21, given the reduced profitability and increased working capital needs.

 

Reduced Exposure to Group Entities: BGSCTPL’s loans and advances declined to INR2.73 billion in 1HFY21 (FY20: INR3.52 billion and FY19: INR2.93 billion). The majority of support was given to Shirke Recreation Enterprise, TSRLLP, PHVR, and Shirke Club Management LLP together accounting for 86% of the total loans and advances at end-1HFY21 (FY20: 93% and FY19: 96%).

 

Additionally, the corporate guarantees extended to group companies have also reduced. BGSCTPL has extended corporate guarantees and letters of undertaking to group entities, which will remain a key rating monitorable over the near-to-medium term.

 

Order Inflow and Execution Slowdown: The order inflows have slowed down considerably in 9MFY21 to INR3.1 billion (FY20: INR7.1 billion) on account of the low order release by the end customers due to procedural delays. Ind-Ra expects the order inflows to pick up in 4QFY21 or FY22. However, continued low order inflows will result in order book depletion and impact the revenue visibility over the long-term. Additionally, in the scenario of low order availability, any bid by BGSCPTL with lower margins could exert pressure on its profitability.

 

Customer and Regional Concentration Remains High: BGSCTPL’s customer concentration remained high at end-December 2020 and the segmental diversification remained limited. CIDCO, DDA,  MHADA, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana accounted for 40%, 22%, 15% and 10%, respectively, of the order book at end-December 2020 (end-October 2019: 39%, 25%, 15%, 10%). Moreover, the concentration of the top eight projects in the order book at end-December 2020 stood at 67% (top 10 projects at end-October 2019: 69%). The orders from Mumbai Metropolitan Region account for 62% of the order book, followed by those from Delhi (22%) and southern India (8%), Pune, Nagpur and Nashik (5%) and others 3%. BGSCTPL continues to have a presence in only the prefabricated housing industry, in line with the management’s strategy to focus on its core strength where the company has a track record of over 30 years. At end-December 2020, work was yet to commence on about 1.6% of the total orders. However, as confirmed by the management, the company has received approvals for the commencement of construction of a majority of projects in its order book.
ratingSensitivities:
Positive: The demonstration of an improvement in the free cash flow (cash flow from operations – interest expenses – capex), resulting in a further improvement in the credit metrics on a sustained basis, a further decline in the support to group entities will be positive for the ratings.


Negative: BGSCTPL’s gross coverage sustaining below 3.0x could lead to a negative rating action.
companyProfile:
Incorporated in 1994 (established business in 1944), BGSCTPL is the flagship company of the Pune-based Shirke Group. BGSCTPL is primarily engaged in the construction of housing projects for government agencies such as DDA, MHADA, CIDCO and Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.

descriptionAboutIndiaRating:
India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) is India's SEBI registered credit rating agency committed to providing India's credit markets accurate, timely, and prospective credit opinions. Built on a foundation of independent thinking, rigorous analytics, and an open and balanced approach towards credit research, Ind-Ra has grown rapidly during the past decade, gaining significant market presence in India's fixed income market.

Ind-Ra currently maintains coverage of corporate issuers, financial institutions (including banks and insurance companies), finance companies, urban local bodies, and structured finance and project finance companies.

Headquartered in Mumbai, Ind-Ra has seven branch offices located in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Pune. Ind-Ra is recognised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India.

Ind-Ra is a 100% owned subsidiary of the Fitch Group.
